vectors.note: the canonical token is emet_self_sha256= (SPEC s.14); the legacy membrane_self_sha256= is also emitted through the 1.x deprecation window
SPEC s.14 deprecation window: the legacy membrane_self_sha256= alias MUST still be emitted at 1.x (removed at 2.0)
inability to read raw bytes is UNVERIFIABLE, never a crash or a default (SPEC sections 3 and 9); both implementations must agree on the error path
refuse on a missing artifact is UNVERIFIABLE with a stable machine reason code, never a crash (SPEC section 9)
both implementations now agree on a space-separated marker (was Python 1 / Rust 0)

a repeated marker counts once per non-overlapping occurrence (SPEC s.16); distinguishes occurrence-counting from distinct-entry counting, which the other refuse vectors do not -- surfaced by the Node.js clean-room implementation
missing corpus is UNVERIFIABLE, not a silent empty denylist
recompute the hash-chained log; a valid chain is INTACT (SPEC sections 7, 13)
a tampered fact whose stored chain no longer recomputes is BROKEN
the chain binds the event kind (SPEC section 7); relabeling kind alone is BROKEN
an implementation writes a hash-chained log entry on anchor and then audits it as INTACT (the write+verify loop, both implementations)
anchor on an unreadable/absent target is UNVERIFIABLE + exit 2, never a silent skip (SPEC s.4); pins the cross-impl behavior an earlier Rust port diverged on (it exited 0)
SPEC s.13 --json envelope: canonical JSON (sorted keys, ', '/': ' separators) carries the governed verdict identically across implementations
the --json envelope reports DRIFT and exit_code 1 (SPEC s.5/s.13)
the --json envelope carries the integer marker count under the SPEC s.13 key
the --json envelope reports the identity under self_sha256 and carries no verdict (selftest is an identity, not a judgement)
SPEC s.9: UNVERIFIABLE carries a stable machine reason code, not prose; verify without an anchor MUST report E_NO_ANCHOR (enforces the enum a prose-emitting impl would fail)
SPEC s.9: an absent target reports reason=E_NOT_FOUND (distinct from E_NO_RAW_CHANNEL for a present-but-unreadable path)
SPEC s.13: spec_version is a governed, byte-compared envelope field; pins its value so every conforming impl agrees
SPEC s.5 precedence: a.txt DRIFTs and b.txt is UNVERIFIABLE (no anchor); the dominant verdict is DRIFT and the exit is 1 (a confirmed difference dominates an inability to check)

SPEC s.7: audit re-derives any conforming log regardless of which impl wrote it. A fact whose path holds a non-BMP/astral char (emoji, stored ASCII-escaped as a UTF-16 surrogate pair) MUST re-serialize identically and audit INTACT; an impl that mishandles surrogate pairs would falsely report BROKEN

SPEC s.7: a log line that cannot be parsed is a tamper event and MUST audit BROKEN (exit 1), not UNVERIFIABLE - a corrupt line is a detected difference from a well-formed chain, never an inability to check

SPEC s.9/s.13: verify is anchor-relative, so a path that is both absent AND unanchored reports reason=E_NO_ANCHOR (the anchor check precedes the read); pins the governed reason so an existence-check-first impl cannot emit E_NOT_FOUND here

SPEC s.9/s.13: the governed coherence reason carries the failing leg - source:<code> or view:<code> - so a consumer can tell which side was unreadable; pins the prefix an impl that drops it would fail
